transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

E:15 on a Bosch dishwasher means the anti-flood system has detected water in the base tray. The drain pump runs continuously on purpose to prevent flooding, so turning it off/on usually will not clear it.

For your SMV4HTX31E:

1. Switch it off at the mains / breaker — not just the front power button.
2. Turn off the dishwasher water supply valve under the sink.
3. Do not run another programme or keep trying resets.
4. Check for obvious water:
• Under the sink around the dishwasher inlet/AquaStop hose connections.
• Around the front bottom edge of the dishwasher.
• Inside the machine: clean the filters and check that nothing is preventing the spray arms or door from sealing properly.

The fault can be caused by a genuine leak (hose, sump, pump seal, door seal, inlet valve etc.), or occasionally water entering the base from an internal overflow/spill. Even if it dries and temporarily resets, the underlying cause still needs finding.

Because it is an integrated machine, avoid pulling it out, tipping it, or dismantling panels unless you are confident and can safely isolate the electrics and plumbing. Tipping it may empty the base tray and stop the pump, but it is not a repair and can cause further water damage.

If there is no obvious external plumbing leak, arrange a Bosch-approved appliance engineer. Tell them: “Bosch SMV4HTX31E, E:15, drain pump running continuously” — that will identify it as an anti-flood/base-water fault.

Filter's fairly clean and there's no water on the floor. The plinth is glued at the ends so I can't take it off, but through a gap I can see a little shine of water in the base tray. I can't pull the unit out either, it's fitted under the worktop.

That confirms E:15: water has reached the dishwasher’s lower safety tray, even if there is none on the kitchen floor.

Keep it isolated:

• Switch off at the wall switch or circuit breaker, not only the dishwasher’s button.
• Turn off its water supply valve.
• Leave it switched off until the water source has been found and repaired.

Do not try to run it, and do not force the cabinet plinth or try to tip the dishwasher while it is installed. Drying the tray may stop the error temporarily, but if the leak remains it will return — potentially with a larger leak.

Since it cannot be pulled out, this is realistically a service/installation-access job. Book Bosch service or a competent appliance engineer and state:

> “Bosch SMV4HTX31E, E:15 anti-flood fault, drain pump continuously running, visible water in base tray; integrated appliance with restricted access.”

They will need to remove the kitchen plinth or release the dishwasher fixing screws (normally fixed to the underside of the worktop or adjacent cabinets), pull the machine forward, dry the base, and identify the leak. Common sources include the inlet/AquaStop system, sump or pump seals, internal hose joints, a loose filter/sump seal, dispenser area, or a door seal/spray-arm issue.

If the plinth is merely siliconed/glued at the ends, it may be intended to come off once the seal is carefully cut, but avoid doing that if it risks damaging the cabinetry. The engineer can advise, or you may need the kitchen fitter/landlord to provide access first.

If water starts appearing outside the appliance or in the cupboard next to it, turn off the home water supply as well and deal with that urgently.
